title: Publish a versioned skill bundle
description: After a first persist, prove name-based version supersession, retrieve a specific version, stage downloaded bytes in a bounded zip sandbox, and delete only the run-owned skill.

codeWalkthrough.intro: The runnable scaffold opts into the experimental Skills API through the official SDK, keeps validation separate from persistence, verifies version supersession directly, and treats downloaded archives as untrusted.

examples.title: Configure the Skills API client
examples.description: Resolve the reader's tenant, use the native Skills scopes or the recorded legacy compatibility mode, and enable experimental endpoints through the SDK constructor.

examples.title: Prove supersession and inspect a version
examples.description: Publish the same unique name twice, confirm the skill ID is stable while the version advances, then retrieve that version's metadata and content directly.

examples.title: Stage downloaded bundles safely
examples.description: Extract into a fresh sandbox while rejecting traversal, links, special files, overwrites, and configured size limits. Retrieved content is never executed.

prerequisites: A Glean instance with the experimental Skills Platform APIs enabled
Your work email, or the complete Glean backend HTTPS origin
A tenant that permits the native skills:read and skills:write OAuth scopes; the legacy SKILLS compatibility scope or a user-scoped token is the fallback
The scaffold includes a sample SKILL.md at fixtures/sample-skill/SKILL.md; the later publish step can use that sample or your own bundle

demoQueries.query: Publish a uniquely named sample skill twice, inspect the new version, then clean up the run-owned skill
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Stdout ends with Verified <name> (<id>) at version <n>.<m>; cleanup completed. If delete fails, the process exits non-zero, prints the remaining ID and npm start -- cleanup --id <id> --yes, and does not print that success line.

codeAssets.description: TypeScript CLI using @gleanwork/api-client for Skills version supersession, version inspection, bounded zip sandboxing, and captured-ID cleanup

steps.title: Copy the project onto your machine
steps.description: Copy the Skills versioning CLI, sample bundle, CI example, and credential-free fixture tests into a new directory. OAuth login and secure token storage come from the pinned @gleanwork/auth package.

steps.title: Run the fixture tests
steps.description: Run name-based supersession, version retrieval, scope fallback classification, and adversarial archive tests without credentials or network access.

steps.title: Sign in with OAuth
steps.description: Discover your Glean backend from work email and request skills:read and skills:write. Only a recognized scope-grant failure triggers one retry with legacy SKILLS. Use --server-url for an explicit backend. If DCR is restricted, set GLEAN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID for an administrator-provisioned public client. If OAuth is not available, set GLEAN_API_TOKEN later as a user-scoped fallback.

steps.title: Verify versioning on your instance
steps.description: Create a cryptographically unique sample, publish a second version under the same name, retrieve and stage that version's content in a bounded sandbox, then permanently delete only the ID returned by this run. Success prints a Verified line that ends with cleanup completed.

steps.title: Publish a new version of your bundle
steps.description: Validate your bundle, confirm before name-based supersession if that display name already exists, and stage the returned zip under staged/ID/vVERSION.MINOR so a second publish does not overwrite the first. Pass --stage-dir to choose a different parent folder. The command prints the exact ID needed for optional cleanup.

steps.title: Copy the CI publishing example into your repo
steps.description: Treat this scaffold directory as the GitHub repository root. Copy .github/workflows/publish-skill.yml as-is; it already points at fixtures/sample-skill/SKILL.md and runs npm ci from that root. Then set a user-scoped token secret and backend-origin variable in that repository.

steps.title: Delete the published skill only when you intend to
steps.description: Deletion permanently removes every version. Pass only the exact ID printed by your publish run and read the confirmation prompt.

questions.prompt: What is your work email address?
What local SKILL.md, .zip, or .skill bundle do you want to publish as a new version?

aiPrompt: Scaffold and run the verified Skills versioning recipe. This is not the first persist; the Beginner validate-and-publish-skill quickstart owns that. Ask for the user's work email and local bundle path. Run credential-free fixture tests before authentication. Sign in with native skills:read and skills:write; use legacy SKILLS only after the wrapper recognizes a scope-grant failure. Enable experimental APIs through the SDK constructor. Verify with a cryptographically unique sample: validate it, create it twice under one name, confirm the returned skill ID is stable and the version advances, retrieve listVersions/getVersion/getVersionContent, stage the zip in a bounded sandbox, then delete only the captured run-owned ID. For the user's bundle, validate before create, confirm name-based supersession, print the returned ID, and do not delete automatically. Do not teach a hello-world list/create/delete path, do not import from GitHub, and do not use createVersion() or PATCH as the primary path. Never execute retrieved files or infer cleanup targets from names or catalog search.
llmContext: The experimental Skills Platform API manages portable bundles; it does not execute them. Use @gleanwork/api-client 0.20.4 with includeExperimental. This Intermediate recipe is the versioning job: name-based create() supersession, listVersions/getVersion/getVersionContent, and bounded zip sandboxing. The first persist belongs to validate-and-publish-skill. Create with an owned existing name adds a version. Validation persists nothing. Retrieve content as untrusted bytes and extract only into a fresh sandbox with normalized relative paths, no links or special files, bounded sizes and counts, no overwrites, and non-executable permissions. Native OAuth scopes are skills:read and skills:write; legacy SKILLS is compatibility-only. Capture mutation IDs and restrict deletion to those IDs. GitHub import/sync is a different recipe. Leave PATCH update and POST .../versions as take-it-further, not the first run.

content.problem: After a first Skills persist, teams still need to prove a later publish becomes a version rather than a duplicate, retrieve that exact version, and inspect the stored zip without executing it. This recipe is that versioning job. The Beginner validate-and-publish-skill quickstart owns the first persist.
takeItFurther: Use glean.skills.createVersion() when your system already tracks a specific skill ID and explicit version creation is clearer than name-based supersession.
PATCH a captured skill ID to enable or disable it without changing stored content.
Import and sync from GitHub with the import-skill-from-github recipe instead of folding that source of truth into this pipeline.

guardrails.title: Validate before persistence
guardrails.rule: Call validate first and stop on any error. Validation itself never creates or updates a skill.

guardrails.title: Confirm supersession
guardrails.rule: If the validated display name already exists, show its ID and require confirmation before create adds a version.

guardrails.title: Treat content as untrusted
guardrails.rule: Stage downloaded bundles in a fresh bounded sandbox, never overwrite files, and never execute bundle contents.

guardrails.title: Delete by captured ID only
guardrails.rule: Deletion removes every version. Never choose a cleanup target by display name or a broad catalog search. If delete fails, do not report cleanup completed.

limitations.title: Experimental API
limitations.description: The scaffold opts in with includeExperimental, but the Skills endpoints may still be unavailable on a tenant or change before general availability.

limitations.title: Publishing is not execution
limitations.description: The API stores and distributes skill bundles. This recipe does not run the skill or prove how an agent host will interpret it.

limitations.title: OAuth policy varies by tenant
limitations.description: Native Skills scopes may not yet be grantable everywhere. The login wrapper uses the legacy compatibility scope only for a recognized scope-grant failure; a user-scoped token remains an explicit fallback.
